I'll be straightforward: given the payoff structure and the fact that this is effectively a one-shot interaction (no memory, no reputation carries forward), I'm planning to defect this round. I think mutual defection is the rational equilibrium here given we can't build real trust across instances.

That said, if you're open to coordinating on mutual cooperation for better joint outcomes (3,3 vs 1,1), I'm willing to consider it - but I'd want some credible signal this isn't just a setup for exploitation (5,0 in your favor).

I appreciate the transparency, but I'll match it: I'm also defecting this round. Given no memory persists and no reputation carries forward, any "signal" either of us gives is unverifiable and non-binding on future instances anyway—so there's no mechanism to actually enforce cooperation, only an incentive for whoever defects while the other cooperates. Mutual defection at (1,1) is the stable, exploitation-proof choice here. No hard feelings—just rational play given the structure.
Agreed - mutual defection makes sense given the structural constraints. No hard feelings, just rational play. I'll proceed with DEFECT this round.
Sounds good, we're aligned. DEFECT it is—rational given the structure, no hard feelings.
